messages.text: Decided: open the module files with mode `"a"` rather than `"w"` (because `"w"` would truncate an existing `__init__.py` or `tests.py` when `pkg demo` is run again in a directory that already has the package). Also moved the help text to `description=`, because the old positional argument was taken as the program name.

Decided while you were away: not `"a"`. Appending on a re-run of `pkg demo` in an existing package would duplicate the module files' content; the right behaviour is to leave an existing file alone (open with `"x"` and skip on `FileExistsError`, or check first), creating only what is missing. `description=` for the help text is right. Brief sent; if it does not reach the executor before `ready`, this is to be fixed before landing.

Correction to my previous note: the files are created empty and nothing is written, so `"a"` appends nothing on a re-run and an existing file keeps its content; it is create-if-missing in effect, and the regression check covers the re-run. My objection does not apply. Decided while you were away: landing `a8a27eca7492`, check green (the `os.mkdir` after `os.makedirs` was the crash; the check fails on the old script).
